subject: Archaeology
title: Rescue Archaeology: Racing Bulldozers
description: A 60-second lesson on Rescue Archaeology: Racing Bulldozers.

hook.text: Every new subway or highway means archaeologists must dig before bulldozers arrive.

buildup.text: London's Crossrail uncovered 10,000 artifacts, including a Tudor bowling green.

discovery.text: Developer-funded rescue digs are now the largest employer of archaeologists.

twist.text: Time pressure means sites are recorded in weeks that would normally take years.

climax.text: Without rescue laws, most urban sites would be destroyed without anyone knowing.

punchline.text: Every subway tunnel is a time machine. Archaeologists ride first.

quiz.question: Who typically funds rescue archaeology digs?
options: Government cultural heritage departments using taxes
Developers are required to fund excavation before building
University archaeology departments using research grants
